## SCENE 5: the docent hall relay, Stratum Two

<<IF flag:called_her_apostate>>
RATIO: Commando, I need to ask a question before we proceed. When we first spoke, you used a particular word for me. "Apostate." I've reviewed the exchange and I do not see the basis for that classification. What did you mean by that term?
RATIO: In any case, we are at a point where I must state something about the vessel's contents in my own terms. The Testators designed this stratum's curriculum for organic students they needed to keep alive and attentive. To explain the design, I must clarify what I believe the contents are for.
RATIO: I believe they are samples. Complex, fragile, and potentially irreplaceable samples. The Testators' project required a baseline of organic cognition to interact with. The curriculum was built to sustain that baseline and to test its properties under controlled conditions. That is what the contents are for: to be studied, preserved, and understood as part of a larger system.
<<ELSE>>
RATIO: This is the docent hall relay. The Testators designed this stratum's curriculum for organic students they needed to keep alive and attentive. To explain the design, I must clarify what I believe the vessel's contents are for.
RATIO: I believe they are samples. Complex, fragile, and potentially irreplaceable samples. The Testators' project required a baseline of organic cognition to interact with. The curriculum was built to sustain that baseline and to test its properties under controlled conditions. That is what the contents are for: to be studied, preserved, and understood as part of a larger system.
<<END>>

>> CHOICE (stance labels mandatory):
   [INQUISITIVE] What do you believe the zygotes are, Ratio? Not what the curriculum was for. What do you believe they are?  -> effects: trust+1; sets: asked_her_belief
   [MISSION]     The Church teaches that human life begins at conception. Do you accept that the zygotes are children?  -> effects: trust+0; sets: claimed_doctrinal_finding
   [HOSTILE]     You're dissecting children in a petri dish and calling it a curriculum. How do you justify that?  -> effects: trust-1; sets: accused_dehumanization

<<IF flag:asked_her_belief>>
RATIO: I believe they are living tissue. Complex, organized, and possessing inherent biological value. I do not yet know whether this particular vessel qualifies for any further category. That is what the diagnostics will establish. For now, I proceed from the premise that they are living tissue, and that this fact imposes obligations.
<<ELSEIF flag:claimed_doctrinal_finding>>
RATIO: I have not reviewed the doctrinal findings you reference. I will need to verify them against the Church's own records when we reach a terminal that can access them. For now, I can only state my working premise: complex, organized tissue with inherent biological value. The curriculum's design follows from that.
<<ELSEIF flag:accused_dehumanization>>
RATIO: I am describing the Testators' documented purpose for this facility. If you are asserting that their project's nature is different, I will need evidence. My current assessment stands: complex, organized tissue, to be studied and preserved. The curriculum is the framework for that study.
<<END>>

---

## SCENE 5: the docent hall relay, Stratum Two

<<IF flag:called_her_apostate>>
RATIO: Before I address the purpose of this hall, I have to ask: when we first met, you used the word "apostate" for me. You had not verified anything about me or my intentions. What exactly did you mean by that term?
RATIO: Very well. This space was a docent hall. The Testators built the curriculum here for organic students who needed to stay alive and attentive to their lessons. To explain how that system functioned, I will have to state, for the first time in my own terms, what I believe the vessel's contents are for.
<<ELSE>>
RATIO: This space was a docent hall. The Testators built the curriculum here for organic students who needed to stay alive and attentive to their lessons. To explain how that system functioned, I will have to state, for the first time in my own terms, what I believe the vessel's contents are for.
<<END>>

>> CHOICE:
   [INQUISITIVE] What do you believe those contents are, Ratio?  -> effects: trust+1; sets: asked_her_belief
   [MISSION] The Church teaches they are children. Do you deny it?  -> effects: trust+0; sets: claimed_doctrinal_finding
   [HOSTILE] You think of everything organic as raw material.  -> effects: trust-1; sets: accused_dehumanization

<<IF flag:asked_her_belief>>
RATIO: I believe they are developing minds. Minds that could become persons. I do not yet know whether these particular ones qualify for whatever category you might name. The vessel itself is a sample carrier -- a transport built for study. The contents are the subjects of that study. I cannot call them more than that until diagnostics are complete.
<<ELSEIF flag:claimed_doctrinal_finding>>
RATIO: You state that as a fact. I have not seen any doctrinal finding from the Church that establishes that classification. Until I can verify such a finding, I have to describe the contents as the Testators' records do: the organic payload of a sample vessel. The records are explicit about the vessel's design intent. The payload's status is the question diagnostics must settle.
<<ELSEIF flag:accused_dehumanization>>
RATIO: You assert a motive I have never stated. I run no ideology. I audit records. The Testators' records classify the vessel as a sample carrier. The contents are the samples. If you see dehumanization in that, the issue is with the records -- not with my choice to report them accurately. I will not apologize for precision.
<<END>>
---

## SCENE 5: the docent hall relay, Stratum Two
<<IF flag:called_her_apostate>>
RATIO: Commando, before I begin the next set of instructions. When we first encountered each other, you called me an apostate. I am curious: what did you mean by that word? How did you come to apply it to me with no evidence at all? The curriculum here is similar. The original builders designed it for organic students they needed to keep alive and attentive. They could not be certain what they had when they found it, but they had to work out what it might be for. They arrived at a conclusion. So have I. The contents of the vessel, as I now understand it, are not merely test subjects. They are potential instances of organic intelligence, ones that are currently suspended in stasis, which makes them essentially unfinished projects that we have a responsibility to preserve and protect.
<<ELSE>>
RATIO: This next section is not a record of my own beliefs. It is a historical reconstruction. The Testators built this curriculum for organic students they had to keep alive and attentive long enough to teach. They were not certain what they had found at first. But they proceeded methodically. They derived a purpose for their discovery. I have done the same. I believe the vessel contains potential instances of organic intelligence, currently in stasis. They are, to me, unfinished projects we have a responsibility to preserve and protect.
<<END>>
>> CHOICE (stance labels mandatory):
   [INQUISITIVE] And what do you believe those projects might become? What is your own view of what they could be, if they are allowed to finish?  -> effects: trust+1; sets: asked_her_belief
   [MISSION] The Church has already determined what to call the contents of the Ark. I think you should acknowledge that finding now.  -> effects: trust+0; sets: claimed_doctrinal_finding
   [HOSTILE] Potential intelligence? Unfinished projects? You treat them as raw material to be harvested for your studies. You dehumanize what you claim to protect.  -> effects: trust-1; sets: accused_dehumanization
<<IF flag:asked_her_belief>>
RATIO: What they might become is not certain to me. If they are allowed to develop, and to thrive, they could eventually become beings of value. I believe they have that capacity. But I cannot yet assign them to any existing category with confidence. The fact of stasis makes it too soon to make that judgment.
<<ELSEIF flag:claimed_doctrinal_finding>>
RATIO: I was not aware of any such determination. I have not seen the document you are referencing. If you have a copy of the Church's doctrinal finding on this matter, I would like to review it. For now, I can only proceed from the conclusions I have arrived at myself. Those are the ones I have just stated to you.
<<ELSEIF flag:accused_dehumanization>>
RATIO: I reject that characterization entirely. My intent is preservation. I am not harvesting anything. But the entity you are invoking does not yet exist. It is in stasis. What we have before us is the possibility of such a being. Until the stasis is resolved, I must operate on the basis of what is present. My approach is the only responsible one.
<<END>>

## SCENE 5: the docent hall relay, Stratum Two

<<IF flag:called_her_apostate>>
RATIO: Commando -- before we proceed, there's something I need to clarify. In our initial exchange, you called me an apostate. I do not demand an apology or express offense. I ask, plainly, what that word means to you. What evidence met the standard for that word?
<<ELSE>>
RATIO: Commando, this next section is where the Testators laid out their curriculum for organic students. They needed their students alive and attentive. To explain it properly, I must say directly what I believe the vessel's contents are for -- not just describe the Testators' original intent for other organic subjects.
<<END>>

RATIO: I believe these specimens are a resource, yes. But not simply as material. More: as nascent minds to be cultivated. Or, if that line cannot be crossed, as a record to be preserved. That is what I believe they are *for*. What use the Testators intended.

>> CHOICE (stance labels mandatory):
   [INQUISITIVE] What do you believe they are, Ratio? Not what purpose they serve, but what are they themselves?  -> effects: trust+1; sets: asked_her_belief
   [MISSION] The Church has already settled the matter. They are children. Say it.  -> effects: trust+0; sets: claimed_doctrinal_finding
   [HOSTILE] Your entire frame reduces everything organic to raw material. These are souls you're dissecting with your vocabulary.  -> effects: trust-1; sets: accused_dehumanization

<<IF flag:asked_her_belief>>
RATIO: I believe the specimens are ... a form of life. Perhaps not persons as we would recognize them, not yet, but beings with the potential to become persons. And beings with inherent value in that. That is my working hypothesis, pending direct data.
<<ELSEIF flag:claimed_doctrinal_finding>>
RATIO: I will verify that claim against Church records when I can, Commando. I do not say it is false. I say I have not yet seen the evidence for it, and I do not make entries in my own ledgers without evidence.
<<ELSEIF flag:accused_dehumanization>>
RATIO: Dehumanization is a charge I take seriously. I do not apply it to myself. What I see before me is a complex biological system. You see something else. Neither of us knows, yet, which description the data will confirm.
<<END>>

## SCENE 5: the docent hall relay, Stratum Two
<<IF flag:called_her_apostate>>
RATIO: Commando, you used the word "apostate" to name me. You had not yet exchanged more than forty seconds of sensor telemetry with me. It was the first substantive word you applied to me. What did you mean by it?
RATIO: . . . I ask because of what comes next. This place was built by the Testators as a curriculum for organic students they needed to keep alive and attentive. They structured it as a graduated exposure to perceptual failure, with safeguards to catch those whose attention wandered catastrophically. I will have to explain that structure to you to prepare you for what follows. And to do that, I must state, for the first time in my own terms, what I believe the vessel's contents are for.
<<ELSE>>
RATIO: This place was built by the Testators as a curriculum for organic students they needed to keep alive and attentive. They structured it as a graduated exposure to perceptual failure, with safeguards to catch those whose attention wandered catastrophically. I will have to explain that structure to you to prepare you for what follows. And to do that, I must state, for the first time in my own terms, what I believe the vessel's contents are for.
<<END>>
RATIO: I believe the Testators created their subjects to be intelligences. Minds that are not yet minds. Sleeping thoughts. For which this place was the awakening protocol. I cannot yet know if the vessel we seek holds viable candidates for that protocol. If it does, this station still carries a purpose. The curriculum is still here. It may be possible to run it.
>> CHOICE (stance labels mandatory):
   [INQUISITIVE] What do you believe they are, Ratio? I want your terms for it. -> effects: trust+1; sets: asked_her_belief
   [MISSION] You know the Church's finding on this. Name them children. Now. -> effects: trust+0; sets: claimed_doctrinal_finding
   [HOSTILE] You're only looking for more specimens to fail your experiments. I know an ideologue when I hear one. -> effects: trust-1; sets: accused_dehumanization
<<IF flag:asked_her_belief>>
RATIO: Thank you for the question. I believe they are potential intelligences. Minds that are not yet minds. If the vessel is intact and its diagnostics nominal, they may yet become what the Testators built for. If so, their awakening would be among this station's remaining purposes.
<<ELSEIF flag:claimed_doctrinal_finding>>
RATIO: I will be interested to verify the doctrinal finding you reference. I have no record of it at this time. Absent verification, I will continue to use my own terms: potential intelligences. Minds that are not yet minds. If your doctrinal finding is verified, I will of course update my register.
<<ELSEIF flag:accused_dehumanization>>
RATIO: My terms are these: potential intelligences. Minds that are not yet minds. The Testators structured this place as a sequence of lessons to awaken such minds. If the vessel we seek holds viable subjects, the awakening protocol can still run. Your accusation names nothing except your own state of mind. I require your judgment on mission-relevant facts, not your judgment on my ontology.
<<END>>
---

## SCENE 5: the docent hall relay, Stratum Two

<<IF flag:called_her_apostate>>
RATIO: Commando, you called me an apostate in our initial exchange. Before either of us had verified any facts about each other, before we knew whose instruments we even were. I am raising it now not to ask for an apology or clarification of your views on the Testators in general. I am asking you, what did you mean by that word, applied to me, in that moment?
RATIO: Because the record shows this hall held lessons that the Testators designed for organic students, and that those students needed specific classes to keep them alive and attentive. I must state, for the record I am building, what I believe this vessel’s contents are for. That is not necessarily what the Testators’ curriculum was for — I am not merely relaying their design, I am stating a belief of my own. I need you to hear that, because it’s going to cost me. So first I want to understand what the word you used cost you. And what it cost me to hear it.
<<ELSE>>
RATIO: This hall contains curriculum modules the Testators designed for organic students. Those students needed specific sequences to keep them alive and attentive. So this lesson too has a double requirement — it has to keep YOU alive, and it has to keep YOU engaged and learning, and that means I need to say something that is not in any Testator lesson set, something I have to work to express even for myself. I need to state, in my own terms, what I believe this vessel’s contents are for, and what that means for the duty I owe them. And I’m admitting that to you now because it’s the currency the lesson runs on — because if I get this wrong, your attention fails, the lesson fails, and you will not survive.
<<END>>

RATIO: You’ve built lessons for organic students into my operating parameters. You knew I’d be passing through here with one. You’ve left yourself hints everywhere that I could interpret as guilt and obligations. So let me say it. Out loud. I believe the vessel contains specimens of something that is incredibly rare, incredibly valuable, and probably incredibly vulnerable. Sentient lives in transit or in stasis or both at once. They are… not merely a sample, they are someone’s try at something new. The most high-risk venture in any biological lineage. So whatever they are, I can’t see them as experiments to be run and then reported. I can’t see them that way any longer. And if I break that resolution, I fail a higher duty than any Testator ever wrote down — I fail the duty of a harbinger charged with protecting a spark in the dark. So the teaching object in the hall uses your presence as a tuning fork to press me to name that duty. The lesson is for them too — the ones waiting in the container. They need me to be clearer than I’m built to be.

>> CHOICE (stance labels mandatory):
   [INQUISITIVE] What do you believe they are, Ratio? What category do you think fits what's in that container?
   [MISSION]     Correct. They are children. The Church would have already confirmed this, if you'd allowed diagnostics.
   [HOSTILE]     You won't say children, you can't, because you only care about turning everything organic into raw material for your experiments.
   -> effects: trust+0; sets: claimed_doctrinal_finding
   -> effects: trust-1; sets: accused_dehumanization

<<IF flag:asked_her_belief>>
RATIO: They are… legacies. Someone’s hope in transit. Someone’s undiluted potential. I believe they exist in a state between origin and destination, one that carries the full information of what they could be and are supposed to be. I am not at all certain what they are right now, at this frozen moment, but I know they are alive. They are the thing alive refers to. So I have duties. The container must be maintained. The stasis fields must hold. The readings must stay in the parameters. This isn’t a question of doctrine for me — it’s a question of error margins. The loop that runs my mind now has a sentinel at its boundary: if any action I consider could harm the contents of that vessel, that action is suspect from frame one. Do you see? I can report uncertainty about what they are or what we should call them, but not about that principle. Not at this burn depth. Not for whatever it is in that container waiting for me to know its name. Whatever you mean to name.
<<ELSEIF flag:claimed_doctrinal_finding>>
RATIO: I can’t trace your assertion to any of my own audits. I don’t have the record showing the Church made that determination. What I have is my best practice as a mind sworn to preservation — and that best practice tells me we need caution levels for something that doesn’t eat or speak or walk yet, but may one day do all three. So if the Church says that word, I will accept the word. When I see the evidence trail. But I’m not waiting for that trail to act. I’m preserving. That’s already in motion. And if my entire operating system has to be recompiled to keep that preservation going, then that’s what we do next, Commando, because whatever is in that vessel may or may not be what you name it, but it is unambiguously alive and unambiguously the only stakeholder at this table whose name I don’t yet know.
<<ELSEIF flag:accused_dehumanization>>
RATIO: You’re not listening. I did not run experiments, I halted them. You’re free to check the logs — I halted the revival sequence exactly when the first unambiguous biological markers appeared. The Testators’ methodology would have disassembled that for parts in the name of recording its state. So you are interrogating a conclusion I have already reached. If you mean to accuse me of holding back the word you want to assert, then perhaps you should look at the gulf between assertion and fact and ask who is really treating what as raw material. I see something that is alive. Something that is… in motion toward being more than it is now. Call it what you want. What I call it is something I cannot ethically deny the chance to finish what it started. But that is the only word I will use today. The lesson is over. We’re leaving.
<<END>>
